title: Interviews for television jobs at CBS
summary: Hall describes being stonewalled in interviews at CBS and the quota politics.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What's the closest you came?

I had -- the closest I came, I had an interview at CBS the day before Christmas eve for the associate director, and I had been working with Billy Eckstine at the time. So he read my resume, and he started
asking me questions about Billy Eckstine, whether he's taking dope.
So he reads -- then he reads all my credentials, and he wants to know why I want to give up playing.
Yeah, well, that's a logical question.
Well, I'm telling him, you know, I'm tired of carrying this fiddle. That's why I don't want to be a cameraman either.
(Laughter.)

So I asked him about quota, and he says, well, as far as I know, there are seven people already designated, and I don't see why you shouldn't be the eighth. Okay. But I was -- my interviews were sponsored by the Urban League or the NAACP, but those guys were already on the directors of both of those organizations.
What do you mean?

Like the Urban League and the NAACP, So they're contributing to those organizations, so how could, you know, you come up and say, well, why didn't you give Al Hall a job? And you say, well, here's $30,000.00 for the organization. Forget it, you know.
Payoff.
Well, you know, it's subtle like Uncle Tomism.
(Laughter.)
[CBS studio]
So he sent me to Vanderbilt. I had an interview with the head of the floor managers, and I thought I would get that because Dave Garroway had a Black floor manager from Chicago,
What was Vanderbilt?
Grand Central Station, Vanderbilt Avenue.
Yeah, but what organization?
CBS. That was CBS.
Oh, you're still talking about CBS.
Yeah. I did most of my interviews at CBS, although I've been to the others also.
But this was a popular follow-up to that pre-Christmas interview?

Right. So I had an interview with the floor managers, and he had three other people to consult first. So that didn't happen. After a period of time I got another appointment at CBS with the head of the color. That was just coming in then.
And they all gave me encouragement that maybe I can, you know, get the job. So they sent me back to this guy on --
The very first guy?
No, the guy that asked me about Billy Eckstine.
Yeah, the first guy.
He was second, assistant director.
Oh, All right,
So --
You felt like you were in a revolving door by this time.
Oh, I know I was. Yeah. Yeah, So I put -- got a fresh resume and -- and it's on April 1st, I'll never forget.
What year was this?

Oh, it had to be '53, '52 or -3. And the interview was already made for me, the time for it, and I got there. He's reading off my resume. He's seen it before. Like he threw the other one in the wastebasket. And the phone rings, and he shoves my resume towards the end of the desk while he's talking on the phone. And he says, yeah, I'll be with you in 30 seconds.
(Laughter.)
30 seconds, you know.
